title: Crown of Aragon
capsule: The Crown of Aragon was a composite monarchy created by the dynastic union of the Kingdom of Aragon and the County of Barcelona in 1137, formally established when Alfonso II became the first ruler to hold both titles in 1162. Under James I 'the Conqueror' (r. 1213–1276) the crown annexed the Balearic Islands and the Kingdom of Valencia, and under Peter III (r. 1276–1285) it gained Sicily after the Sicilian Vespers uprising of 1282; by the fourteenth century it controlled a maritime empire including Sardinia, Naples, and parts of mainland Greece. The Crown of Aragon merged with the Crown of Castile through the inheritance of Charles I (Holy Roman Emperor Charles V) in 1516, forming the foundation of the Spanish monarchy, though Aragonese institutions persisted until the Nova Planta decrees of 1707–1716.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Iberian core of the Crown of Aragon is well documented through extensive royal archives; Mediterranean possessions and their changing extent are well attested, though internal jurisdiction boundaries between component kingdoms are complex.
